gap_analysis.miniork_today: mini_ork/recipes_catalog.py:174 lists recipes only under <home>/recipes and the engine recipes/ dir, with project shadowing at :241; mini_ork/cli/main.py:48-78 has no recipes subcommand.
gap_analysis.gap: No remote index, version/checksum metadata, install destination or source prefix; sharing requires a git clone or manual copy.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: docs/EXTENSION.md:26 tells authors to copy a shipped recipe; recipes/recipe-creator/ is an LLM-driven recipe; mini_ork/cli/validate.py:407 validates a project, not a recipe directory.
gap_analysis.gap: No deterministic recipe init, template set or recipe validate/pack contract; the schema already lags the live dialect per docs/EXTENSION.md:32.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: recipes are self-contained dirs (recipes/code-fix/ ships task class, workflow, artifact contract, prompts, verifiers, probes) and recipe-local register.py is loaded by mini_ork/cli/recipe_register.py.
gap_analysis.gap: No bundle manifest, deterministic pack command or install/unpack path; the format is defined by convention, not schema.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: No migrate subcommand in mini_ork/cli/main.py:48-78; skills can be copied into .agents/skills or $MINI_ORK_HOME/config/skills; kickoffs are plain Markdown.
gap_analysis.gap: No preview/apply plan model, source detection, conflict handling or migration-provider registration seam.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: Six register_* seams (providers.py:916, execute_handlers.py:3424, gate_registry.py:332, main.py:2203, features/registry.py:212, routing.py:336, semantic.py:178) documented in docs/EXTENSION.md.
gap_analysis.gap: No versioned compatibility policy, per-seam stability labels or introspection command proving what is registered in a process.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: recipes_catalog.list_recipes returns every visible recipe with description and task class; task_class.yaml carries matches.keywords; the IDE thread pages consume it.
gap_analysis.gap: No user-facing recipes list/search CLI; discovery is only reachable through the IDE/thread session surfaces.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: config/providers.yaml is one hand-maintained registry with several kind values; mini_ork/dispatch/providers.py:916 accepts new kinds; mini-ork providers status/configure handles credentials.
gap_analysis.gap: No per-provider files/packages, catalog command with docs URLs, or per-lane health matrix; adding a provider is a core config edit.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, GOVERNANCE.md, MAINTAINERS.md, two issue templates, a PR template and CI exist.
gap_analysis.gap: CONTRIBUTING.md:19-27,58-70 still documents the removed bash runtime (tests/smoke.sh, shellcheck, bash arrays); no recipe/plugin proposal route, curated good-first-issue section, or pre-PR review skill.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: config/vault.example.yaml demonstrates the simple/secure two-tier pattern; mini_ork/cli/skills.py:97 validates skill frontmatter; recipes are local and unreviewed by construction.

gap_analysis.miniork_today: mini_ork/dispatch/skill_registry.py resolves SKILL.md directories across run/operator/project tiers and .agents/skills; mini-ork skills list/show/validate/promote exists at mini_ork/cli/skills.py:212-228; docs/CONFIG.md:471 documents grants and precedence.
gap_analysis.gap: No search, install, publish or remote index; the registry is local-only.

open_questions: Where should community recipes live: a separate registry repo, or PRs to recipes/? If recipes stay in-tree, E1 and E3 drop in value and E2/E6 dominate.
Who is the primary audience: agent-workflow developers authoring recipes, or ops teams wiring providers/gates? The former ranks E2/E1/E3 above E7; the latter ranks E7/E9 higher.
Can mini-ork support arbitrary recipe code safely? Recipe-local register.py and verifier scripts are code execution; without a sandbox or review bar, E1/E3 need curation or a trust model.
Is there an existing distribution channel (PyPI packages, GitHub templates) that makes a new registry redundant? If so, E1 shrinks to a thin index and E3 becomes the main artifact.
Do Claude Code / Codex skill authors want a second registry, or is GitHub enough? If GitHub is enough, E10 shrinks to a documented import path absorbed by E4.
What is the maintainer capacity for review? A registry with no review is worse than none, and the answer decides whether E1 launches open or curated.
